resources.string: Memory, processor time and loaded models, and unload what you don\'t need
memory ram cpu battery process monitor task manager unload model

This is the memory the whole keyboard uses right now, as Android counts it for the App info page. Android doesn\'t split it by feature. The parts below are the kinds of memory, and a loaded model shows up mostly as native memory or graphics.
%1$s allocated by native code right now

Processor time is the closest thing to battery use that Android lets an app measure for itself. It is counted per thread, and threads are grouped by their names, so a model that runs on threads it named shows up under Models. Time on threads that have already ended counts only in the total.

What is in memory right now. The size is the size of the model file, which is a fair estimate of what it holds, and a model can hold more while it works. Unloading frees the memory at once. The model loads again the next time you use it, which takes a moment and uses some battery. The keyboard also unloads everything by itself 2 minutes after it hides.
No models are loaded right now.
Also drops decoded icons, thumbnails and open dictionaries that the keyboard rebuilds as it needs them.
%1$s in a process of its own. It unloads its model a few minutes after you last use it.
Files the keyboard keeps to work faster and can always make again. Android may clear them by itself when storage runs low.
The parts of the app that Android is running as services at the moment. The keyboard itself is one of them while it is your keyboard.
Reading the screen for the floating button

Android works out battery use per app and keeps it to itself, so no app can see its own share split by feature. Processor time above is the honest stand-in: the busier a part, the more it costs.\n\nWith Shizuku, or with root allowed in the app launcher\'s settings, the keyboard can read Android\'s own estimate of what it used since the last full charge, split into processor, network and the rest. That is still an estimate made by Android\'s power model, not a measurement. Without either, open the system\'s battery usage page.
